Column-lineage dataset facet

Source: R/ol-facets.R
column_lineage_facets.Rd

Constructors for column-level lineage: which input columns each output column of a dataset was computed from, and which input columns affect the whole dataset.

Usage

ColumnLineageTransformation(
  type,
  subtype = NULL,
  description = NULL,
  masking = NULL
)

ColumnLineageInputField(namespace, name, field, transformations = list())

ColumnLineageDatasetFacet(
  fields = list(),
  dataset = list(),
  producer = OPENLINEAGE_PRODUCER,
  deleted = NULL
)

Arguments

type

The transformation type, such as "DIRECT" or "INDIRECT".

subtype

An optional transformation subtype, such as "IDENTITY". May be empty, as the specification allows.

description

An optional description of the transformation. May be empty, as the specification allows.

masking

An optional flag: whether the transformation masks the data.

namespace, name

The input dataset namespace and name.

field

The input column name.

transformations

An unnamed list of ColumnLineageTransformation objects.

fields

A named list keyed by output column name. Each element is an unnamed list of ColumnLineageInputField objects.

dataset

An unnamed list of ColumnLineageInputField objects that affect the whole dataset, such as filter, sort, grouping or join keys.

producer

A URI identifying the facet producer.

deleted

Whether this facet deletes a previously emitted facet.

Value

A column-lineage facet, input-field or transformation S7 object.

Details

fields is keyed by output column name. Each element is an unnamed list of ColumnLineageInputField objects, possibly empty, and serializes as {"inputFields": [...]}. The facet is usually attached to an output dataset under the key columnLineage.

The specification describes type as "DIRECT" or "INDIRECT" and leaves subtype free. OpenLineage documents "IDENTITY", "TRANSFORMATION" and "AGGREGATION" for direct transformations and "JOIN", "GROUP_BY", "FILTER", "SORT", "WINDOW" and "CONDITIONAL" for indirect ones. Both are typed as free strings in the JSON schema, so other values are accepted, as in the Python client. The deprecated per-column transformationDescription and transformationType properties are not supported.

See also

https://openlineage.io/spec/facets/1-2-0/ColumnLineageDatasetFacet.json

Examples

direct <- ColumnLineageTransformation("DIRECT", "IDENTITY", masking = FALSE)
filter <- ColumnLineageTransformation("INDIRECT", "FILTER")
customers <- function(field, transformation) {
  ColumnLineageInputField(
    "postgres://warehouse",
    "public.customers",
    field,
    list(transformation)
  )
}
facet <- ColumnLineageDatasetFacet(
  fields = list(customer_name = list(customers("name", direct))),
  dataset = list(customers("active", filter))
)
OutputDataset(
  "postgres://warehouse",
  "analytics.customers",
  facets = list(columnLineage = facet)
)
#> <openlineage::OutputDataset>
#>  @ namespace    : chr "postgres://warehouse"
#>  @ name         : chr "analytics.customers"
#>  @ facets       :List of 1
#>  .. $ columnLineage: <openlineage::ColumnLineageDatasetFacet>
#>  ..  ..@ producer  : chr "https://github.com/pedrobtz/openlineage"
#>  ..  ..@ schema_url: chr "https://openlineage.io/spec/facets/1-2-0/ColumnLineageDatasetFacet.json#/$defs/ColumnLineageDatasetFacet"
#>  ..  ..@ deleted   : NULL
#>  ..  ..@ fields    :List of 1
#>  .. .. .. $ customer_name:List of 1
#>  .. .. ..  ..$ : <openlineage::ColumnLineageInputField>

#>  .. .. ..  .. ..@ name           : chr "public.customers"
#>  .. .. ..  .. ..@ field          : chr "name"

#>  .. .. .. .. .. .. $ : <openlineage::ColumnLineageTransformation>

#>  .. .. .. .. .. ..  ..@ subtype    : chr "IDENTITY"
#>  .. .. .. .. .. ..  ..@ description: NULL

#>  ..  ..@ dataset   :List of 1
#>  .. .. .. $ : <openlineage::ColumnLineageInputField>
